about: While the consultant is building, a message the client writes opens a TALKER:
a second round of the consultant that converses while the first — the worker —
carries on. The talker is offered the same tools as the worker, so the two
share one cached prefix, but a tool named in `withhold` returns `refusal`
instead of running. The framework always adds `Status`.
`withhold` is the worker's: everything that changes the draft or moves the
progress stages. The talker is only talking; the stage is determined by the
work being done, and the draft has one writer at a time. `allow` is everything
else the consultant may be granted: the story board, panel questions and the
facts and decisions the client gives, comps, web search and reading the site.
The story board is allowed even while a builder writes the related copy — it
is background material, never the site.
EVERY TOOL THE CONSULTANT CAN BE GRANTED IS IN EXACTLY ONE LIST. A UAT composes
the consultant's real grant, with the consultant's own writes switched on and
off, and fails on a tool in neither — so a new tool is classified when it is
added rather than reaching the talker by default.
The settings assistant has no talker setting and is never forked.
refusal: That's part of the build that's running; I'll pick it up as soon as it's done.
